provenance: Factory baseline: the source rules applied before a restore installs dependencies. When a new commonly used source appears in the ecosystem, ship it through the rules update; no CLI release is needed.
note: The allowlist is not a hard security boundary -- anyone can host a wheel on the large code and model hosts. What it stops is targeted poisoning that points at an unfamiliar host, narrowing the attack surface to ecosystems where publishers have an identity, can be held responsible, and can be taken down. The real boundary is the user's own judgement about where a nest came from. **Public wording must never imply that being on the allowlist means being safe.**
no_wildcards_note: Wildcard suffixes are deliberately unsupported. They look convenient, but a pattern like `*.example-storage.com` would admit every user's bucket on that provider, so an attacker only has to register one. Incompleteness is covered three ways instead: rules updates, an environment variable, and an explicit override flag. Anyone tempted to add wildcards should read this first.
cn_mirrors_note: The mirror entries are required, not optional: our own installation instructions for that region set the package index to a mirror, and the machine templates there use mirrors throughout. Without these entries, a user who follows our own documentation would install successfully and then be unable to restore. Where singular and plural host spellings are both plausible, both are listed: an extra host name that does not exist costs nothing (it never matches), while a missing real one blocks a user -- and all of these sit under domains their operators control, so an attacker cannot register a subdomain of them.
unverified_note: These entries were added from documentation rather than confirmed by resolving them on a clean network. The asymmetry above absorbs the risk (a wrong entry never matches; a missing one blocks a user), and a verification pass on a clean network is still worth doing.
scope_note: This gate **covers only the URLs declared in the dependency lock** -- where packages are installed from. It is not egress control: model blobs go through our own downloader with sha256 verification and never pass through here. It also only inspects the string declared in the lock, not where a redirect leads. Therefore content-delivery endpoints, model-hosting CDNs and pre-signed object-storage domains **must never be added to this list**: putting an object-storage domain on a package-install allowlist means anyone who can create a bucket and host a malicious wheel passes the gate.
no_perf_cost_note: A useless entry costs nothing: the audit is a set comparison and issues no network request. "One more domain, one more timeout" applies to racing blob sources, not here. So when in doubt, keep the entry rather than trimming it away.
hosts_note: Where these came from: no outside authority publishes such a list, so every entry is a decision of ours -- the package indexes, code hosts and model hosts real dependency locks point at, plus the regional mirrors our own instructions tell people to use. That is why this table replaces rather than merges when it is refreshed: the day a host turns bad, we have to be able to take it out, and a merging table cannot be shrunk. Adding one is a judgement call and needs the reason written into the commit, not a measurement: read scope_note and no_wildcards_note above before adding anything.
